title: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge Technical Research White Paper — Architecture, Methodology & Validation Framework
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge Technical Research White Paper — Architecture, Methodology & Validation Framework Overview This white paper documents NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™ v16.0.0, an implemented local-first health-information retrieval and contextual discovery system developed within the NHOS Intelligence Matrix Engine™ (NIME™) research program. The system composes hybrid lexical/fuzzy retrieval, multi-concept Matrix processing, on-device NLP normalization, concept-graph-assisted expansion, isotonic confidence calibration, deployment-state transparency, cross-tab federated synchronization, and browser-native voice input into a single architecture for personal health knowledge discovery. The paper is the first public publication documenting the complete v6.3 → v16.0.0 evolution in a single revision. It supersedes five previously unpublished internal drafts (v1.0–v1.4) and reconciles the historical record across the v6.3 baseline, the v7.x Scientific/Modular lineage, and the v8.x NLP/Localization/Deployment-State lineage. What This Paper Documents Part I — Research Foundation: Problem definition, research gap, 20 research questions (RQ1–RQ20), 8 research objectives, scope and delimitations, and architectural positioning within NIME™. Part II — Oracle Architecture & Retrieval: Ten-layer system architecture, knowledge aggregation pipeline, index construction, query processing pipeline, normalization/tokenization/query planning, exact and fuzzy matching, Porter stemmer, concept ontology, category weighting, synonym expansion, ontology expansion, type-specific boosting, ranking and scoring, algorithmic confidence, waterfall explanation, isotonic calibration, and the NHOS Matrix Engine. Part III — Matrix & Recommendation Intelligence: Multi-concept query parsing, concept extraction, Matrix matching, matched-concept tracking, Matrix confidence/coverage, Matrix-vs-Hybrid comparison, graph traversal, local interaction history, session context, recommendation generation pipeline, deterministic candidate selection, intelligence layer (herb actions, symptom clusters, evidence inference), and recommendation influence. Part IV — Application/Interaction Architecture: Local search analytics, configuration panel, search history panel, autocomplete, voice search pipeline, voice-query correction, filtering/sorting/facets/clustering, Clinical Mode and v16 clinical scoring boosts, knowledge discovery routing, saved knowledge, export architecture (CSV/PDF/JSON/XML/DOCX/FHIR R4), sharing, and local-first architecture. Part V — Local-First Infrastructure: Local persistence, offline architecture, SHA-256 corpus integrity verification, privacy model, security boundaries, data lifecycle, implementation status, and local telemetry. Part VI — Evidence Discipline & Safety: Explicit non-claims, known technical limitations, failure modes, safety boundaries, and the distinction between implementation and empirical validation. Part VII — Scientific Evaluation: Evaluation framework, benchmark dataset design, human relevance judgment protocol, precision/recall, MRR/nDCG, confidence calibration, Matrix Engine evaluation, ablation studies, baseline comparisons, recommendation evaluation, privacy/network evaluation, offline evaluation, performance evaluation, scalability evaluation, and error analysis. Part VIII — Research Program: Reproducibility artifact contract, reproducibility protocol, embedded test suite (17 assertions), research roadmap, Q4 2026–Q2 2027 validation program, 23 research contributions, relationship to NIME™, future research, explainable retrieval, scientific interpretation, and conclusion. Appendices A–N: Core terminology, hybrid retrieval pipeline, Matrix Engine pipeline, proposed validation matrix, evidence classification, publication integrity statement, research position, implementation status matrices, benchmark specification template, validation record template, v6.3 → v16.0.0 changelog, Zenodo deposit metadata, and version history summary. Key Architectural Subsystems (v16.0.0) Subsystem Description Hybrid Retrieval Exact/content, title/excerpt, token-level, Levenshtein fuzzy (≤2), category weighting, type-specific boosting NHOS Matrix Engine Delimiter-based multi-concept parsing (5 delimiter classes), concept-by-concept matching, matched-concept tracking, coverage-based confidence NLP Normalization Layer Porter stemmer, ~40-entry curated synonym map, Levenshtein-based voice-query correction Concept Ontology 37-concept starter graph across 8 branches, graph-distance ranking boost (8 × 0.5^(d/halfLife)), regex-based relation extraction Query Planner Negation parsing, type-hint extraction, comparative operators, temporal markers Session Context 10 recent queries / 20 selections, JSON export/import Facets & Clustering Type/Category/Evidence refinement, TF-IDF k-means (k=5, hash-seeded centroids) Waterfall Explanation Per-category score contribution bars Vector Projection 256-dim hash-based (opt-in), L2-normalized, cosine similarity Extensibility Custom scorers, plugin system (5 hooks), query rewrites, local telemetry Isotonic Calibration Pool-adjacent-violators regression, opt-in, requires ≥30 labeled samples Federated Sync Five-source boot cascade (parent → localStorage → BroadcastChannel → server → embedded), CRDT primitives (Lamport, G-Set, LWW-Register), AES-GCM + PBKDF2 encrypted sync, cross-tab coordination, federation protocol Deployment-State Reporting Sync-state indicator (standalone / syncing / synchronized / synced-with-peers) Internationalization 7 languages (en, es, fr, de, it, pt, nl), configurable fallback chain, per-language coverage reporting Discoverability Static structured-data metadata (6 JSON-LD blocks), hreflang alternates, PWA manifest — no runtime telemetry Evidence Status NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™ is an implemented research system. This paper documents its architecture, retrieval methodology, implemented capabilities, and proposed evaluation framework. Implementation status should not be interpreted as empirical validation. The paper intentionally does not claim: Superior retrieval performance Superior ranking quality Clinical effectiveness or diagnostic accuracy Recommendation effectiveness Calibrated confidence (except where explicitly fitted and evaluated) Reduced health-information errors or improved health outcomes Superiority to semantic/vector retrieval, BM25, or TF-IDF Privacy or security superiority Speech-recognition accuracy superiority Stemmer, synonym-coverage, ontology-coverage, or clustering-quality superiority Cross-tab sync reliability under adversarial conditions Measurably improved discoverability from the SEO block Statistically significant user benefit These are research hypotheses or validation targets scheduled for Q4 2026 – Q2 2027. Reproducibility A reproducible run of Oracle must record, at minimum: Engine version, build, schema version, corpus version Confidence method, routing triggers i18n language and fallback chain Stemming, synonym expansion, voice correction status Ontology loaded, concept count, coverage Vector projection active, vector count Clustering enabled Custom scorer count, plugin count Calibration blocks Item count Parent-sync status, sync state, sync source Last routing path Deterministic recommendations Voice supported Build type The canonical capture method is NHOSOracleHybridSearch.getStats(), which returns a plain JSON-serializable object independent of DOM state. Embedded test suite: NHOSOracleHybridSearch.runTests() executes 17 pure-function assertions; the shipped v16.0.0 build reports 17/17 passed. Companion Artifacts JAMIA Pilot Evaluation Package — 30-item curated corpus, 120-query benchmark spanning ten query categories, in-browser evaluation script, and human relevance-judgment template. Submitted for review at the Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association; results are not reported in this document. tools.html Corpus Publisher — Companion script that broadcasts NHOS host databases to any Oracle instance on the same origin. Structured-Data Metadata Block — Static metadata for search-engine discoverability; no runtime telemetry. Software Availability Public implementation: https://nhos.health/oracle/ Engine: NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine v16.0.0 Entry point (single-file): oracle_v16.html, self-contained Entry point (modular, strict CSP): oracle_v16.html + oracle.css + oracle.js No server, no build step, no network access required for core retrieval Runtime provenance: Call NHOSOracleHybridSearch.getStats() in the browser console Regression harness: Call NHOSOracleHybridSearch.runTests() Verification: scripts/verify-hashes.sh verifies vendor and corpus integrity Standalone sync: Auto-synchronizes from /oracle/data/corpus.json, from localStorage, or from any open tools.html tab on the same origin License Paper text: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Software: No license is asserted in the paper; the software deposit carries its own license. How to Cite NHOS Labs, Inc. (2026). NHOS Oracle Matrix Search Engine™: A Local Hybrid Retrieval, Ontology-Aware, and Federated Sync Architecture for Personal Health Knowledge (White Paper v2.0, corresponding to software v16.0.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22775626 Data Availability No empirical datasets are associated with this revision. The JAMIA pilot evaluation package includes a 30-item corpus and a 120-query benchmark; both are deposited separately and linked from the software deposit. cited_by.title: NHOS Intel™ v4.1 — A Local-First Personal Health Intelligence, Research Intelligence, Evidence Integration, NHOS Interoperability Architecture and Insight Engine
cited_by.abstract: NHOS Intel™ v4.1 — Personal Health Intelligence, Research Intelligence, Evidence Integration, and NHOS Interoperability Architecture NHOS Intel™ v4.1 is a browser-based, local-first personal health intelligence and research platform developed as part of the NHOS™ (Natural Health Operating System) ecosystem. The platform integrates longitudinal personal health context, deterministic health-information processing, structured knowledge retrieval, evidence and provenance handling, research workflows, analytical tools, interoperability services, and privacy-preserving local computation within a unified client-side application. This technical white paper documents the architecture, implementation, feature system, interoperability model, evidence architecture, research platform, privacy and security design, verification methodology, deployment model, limitations, and future research directions of NHOS Intel™ v4.1. The publication is intended to provide a reproducible architectural and implementation record for researchers, software engineers, digital-health developers, health-information researchers, and other technical reviewers studying local-first health-information systems. System Architecture NHOS Intel™ is organized around a layered architecture in which NIME™ (NHOS Intelligence Matrix Engine™) functions as the intelligence core, NHOS Intel™ provides the principal user-facing intelligence interface, and the broader NHOS ecosystem provides specialized applications and engines connected through the NHOS Handshake Protocol (NHOS-HS). The architecture separates the intelligence, interface, application, evidence, personal-context, and interoperability concerns while allowing them to operate together as an integrated local-first environment. NHOS-HS provides application discovery, capability registration, version compatibility, contextual navigation, request/response messaging, acknowledgements, provenance, permission boundaries, and controlled transfer of application context. The paper documents both NHOS-HS/1.0 and the subsequent NHOS-HS/1.1 extension architecture, including the registered NHOS application ecosystem and the mechanisms used to coordinate NIME, NHOS Intel, Oracle, Clinical Symptom Intelligence, Interaction Checker, Protocol Generator, Remedy Revealer, MedSyn, Track, Integrity Checker, Children's Symptoms Checker, Evidence, and other NHOS applications. Personal Health Intelligence NHOS Intel™ provides a longitudinal personal-health environment for organizing and interpreting locally maintained health context. The platform includes Health Journal, Intel Memory, Sleep Intelligence, Timeline, Pattern Explorer, Compare, Cross-Check, Insight Engine, Advanced Analytics, Prediction and Forecasting, Daily Routine, Protocol Builder, Data Quality, Encrypted Vault, and related contextual tools. Personal health information is designed to remain within the user's local application environment unless an explicitly authorized interoperability operation permits its use by another NHOS component. The architecture therefore treats personal health context as a controlled information domain rather than as unrestricted application data. The platform also provides mechanisms for importing health information, maintaining local records, generating reports, exporting structured information, and preserving longitudinal context for subsequent local analysis. Research Platform A central component of NHOS Intel™ v4.1 is its integrated Research Platform, which extends the application beyond personal health tracking into structured health-information research and evidence exploration. Research functionality includes knowledge-base access, evidence-oriented retrieval, evidence overview, record comparison, evidence-quality analysis, cross-checking, research traceability, citation and provenance handling, and controlled interaction with the broader NHOS research ecosystem. The Research Platform is designed to maintain a distinction between personal health context and research/knowledge resources. This separation allows NHOS Intel™ to provide research-oriented information without treating research records as personal clinical data or presenting research outputs as individualized medical diagnoses. Knowledge and Evidence Architecture NHOS Intel™ incorporates a structured knowledge architecture supported by successive knowledge-base expansion packs. The documented implementation includes Knowledge Base Expansion Packs #1–#6 and additional research, reliability, accessibility, analytics, prediction, caregiver, and interoperability feature packages. The platform provides mechanisms for structured retrieval, record construction, evidence linkage, provenance preservation, citation handling, and knowledge-base auditing. Citation and provenance mechanisms are intended to make the origin and transformation of information inspectable rather than presenting generated or retrieved information as an unexplained output. The white paper documents the platform's evidence model, citation-resolution architecture, KB Audit functionality, Evidence Overview, Evidence Quality, Cross-Check, and Research Trace mechanisms. Deterministic Intelligence The Ask Intel subsystem implements a documented multi-stage deterministic processing pipeline for interpreting user requests against the available local knowledge and evidence environment. The architecture emphasizes explicit processing stages, structured retrieval, record construction, evidence association, contextual interpretation, and response formation rather than presenting the system as an opaque generative model. The publication documents the distinction between evidence matching, contextual interpretation, and confidence presentation. Confidence indicators within the platform are not presented as probabilities of disease and are not intended to constitute clinical diagnostic probabilities. Analytics, Patterns, and Prediction NHOS Intel™ includes analytical functionality for longitudinal health-context exploration, including Advanced Analytics, Pattern Explorer, trend analysis, anomaly-oriented observations, and prediction/forecasting features. These capabilities are documented as computational and informational functions operating on available local data. The paper explicitly distinguishes such analytical outputs from clinical diagnosis, medical prognosis, or independently validated clinical prediction. The architecture is therefore presented as a health-information intelligence environment rather than as a clinically validated diagnostic or prognostic system. Clinical Screening and Safety Boundaries The platform incorporates standardized screening workflows and red-flag-oriented functionality while maintaining explicit boundaries between screening, informational interpretation, and diagnosis. The documented implementation includes support for standardized instruments and screening workflows, including PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI, STOP-BANG, and PSS-10, together with red-flag triage and safety-oriented interface behavior. These functions are documented as informational and screening-oriented capabilities. They do not constitute independent clinical validation, diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or replacement of professional medical evaluation. Privacy and Local-First Design Privacy preservation is a foundational architectural principle of NHOS Intel™. The platform is designed around local browser execution, local persistence, controlled application interoperability, explicit permissions for personal-health-context transfer, and minimal dependence on remote infrastructure for core functionality. The architecture includes an encrypted local vault, data-quality controls, explicit context permissions, controlled NHOS-HS messaging, and mechanisms intended to prevent unauthorized transfer of personal health context between applications. The publication distinguishes the handling of personal health information from operational mechanisms such as application interoperability, error handling, and externally accessible research resources. Privacy claims are therefore framed in terms of the documented implementation and its defined boundaries rather than as an unrestricted assertion that no network activity can ever occur. Interoperability NHOS Intel™ functions as an interoperability interface within the NHOS ecosystem through NHOS-HS. The documented protocol supports application registration, discovery, capabilities, version compatibility, navigation, request identifiers, acknowledgements, provenance, context exchange, permission boundaries, BroadcastChannel-based communication, and browser postMessage communication where applicable. The interoperability architecture enables specialized NHOS applications to remain independently deployable while participating in a coordinated health-intelligence environment. Accessibility and Internationalization The platform includes accessibility-oriented functionality, voice interaction, keyboard and focus support, multilingual interface infrastructure, and right-to-left language support. Documented language and internationalization capabilities include English, French, Spanish, and Arabic/RTL-oriented interface support. These features are implemented as part of the application architecture rather than as external accessibility documentation alone. Data Exchange, Reporting, and Portability NHOS Intel™ includes mechanisms for health-data import, structured export, FHIR R4-oriented data exchange, calendar-oriented export, PDF report generation, Web Share integration, and Progressive Web App functionality. The platform is designed to remain useful as a self-contained browser application and supports offline-oriented operation after the required application resources have been loaded. Verification and Reproducibility The white paper documents a source-based verification methodology combining static implementation inspection, runtime execution,
